about: The processes of a workspace deployment (infrastructure design §3.1), the one list the Helm chart and the Compose file are both rendered from (E21-36). A process renders only when values.images names its image, so a lane adds its process by building the image; nothing else changes. `built` says whether the process's image exists yet: the Compose file holds exactly the built processes, less any whose `compose` is false, which have no Compose adapter (the deployment manager drives Kubernetes only, DEC-1172), or none yet (the scheduler and the data process, until the Compose drill builds their images, E21-29). A process whose `started_by` names another is not a Deployment of its own once that process renders: the chart renders its pod into that process's templates instead, and that process starts it (DEC-1170), with `run --probe /tmp/process.sock` and its `probe`; its `args` start it only where that process does not render. A `one_shot` process it starts (the token exchange, DEC-1175) runs its `command` and `args`, `{vault}` the vault's address, with no probe, once; the token exchange reads its connection from `MANDATE_SUBJECT`. A `vault_token` process mounts a projected ServiceAccount token for the vault (audience `mandate-vault`, 600 seconds, at `/run/mandate/vault-token/token`), beside its namespace at `/run/mandate/vault-token/namespace`, and no other credential (DEC-2060, DEC-1177), only as a pod the deployment manager starts as its connection's own account, and the executor only where its broker reaches the vault (DEC-2336). A `vault_ca` process mounts the vault chart's CA certificate alone, the ConfigMap `vault-ca`, read-only at `/run/mandate/vault/ca.crt`; the executor only when its broker reaches the vault (DEC-2332 item 5). A service's `args` start it and its `probe` asks it `livez` or `readyz` over its socket on the pod's `/tmp` (DEC-994 item 5); `{workspace}`, `{hosted_workspace}` (`api.workspace`, the workspace the deployment manager hosts), `{data_instruments}`, the `data.instruments` list as `<symbol>:<assetId>:<anchor>` comma-separated, and the `runtime` values' `{agent}`, `{connection}` and `{owner}` fill them (DEC-1013). Edit this file, then run `cargo xtask cell generate --write`, which writes the Compose file and the journal's roles file from it.

processes.name: migrate
processes.row: The migration Job (§7.2, OPS-13): forward-only SQL from migrations/ under the migration-owner role, before processes roll, never at start

processes.name: control
processes.row: Workspace control services, Phase 1: the founder's CLI, run as a one-off Job (§3.1)

processes.name: connect-check
processes.row: The executor's connect check of a paper connection (connections spec §8.1), run as a one-off Job: Postgres only, on the in-process fixture broker, with no credential (DEC-2035)

processes.name: journal-verify
processes.row: A `mandate journal export` then `mandate journal verify` of each named stream (journal spec §11), as a one-off Job

processes.name: api
processes.row: Workspace API server (workspace API spec §3.11, DEC-978): Postgres and the identity provider's key set; it listens on its pod's loopback only, so nothing in the cluster reaches it until the tunnel's route lands

processes.name: deploy-manager
processes.row: Deployment manager, one per workspace (infrastructure design §3.4, DEC-1170, DEC-1172): Postgres and the cluster's API server, through a service account whose one Role creates, reads, lists and deletes pods in its own namespace; it starts every runtime and executor from the chart's pod templates. Kubernetes only, so it is not in the Compose file

processes.name: role-provisioner
processes.row: Role provisioner, one per workspace (DEC-2350, DEC-2630 item 7): Postgres and the vault only. It makes each OAuth connect's Kubernetes-auth roles and removes the token exchange's, logged in by its own AppRole, and journals each on the control stream; it holds no service-account token and no broker credential. Kubernetes only, since its roles bind the workspace's ServiceAccounts, so it is not in the Compose file

processes.name: connect-finish
processes.row: Connect finish (`mandate-api-server finish`, DEC-2348 item 3): Postgres and the vault only. It finishes each OAuth connect on the control stream, deletes a closed connect's code and token, and judges and releases its account's fingerprint, logged in by the connection manager's AppRole alone; it listens on nothing. Rendered with `api.connectFinish`, from the API's image. Kubernetes only, so it is not in the Compose file

processes.name: runtime
processes.row: Agent runtime, one per agent deployment: no broker credential and no route to a broker (rule 12); on the deny-all wiring until the post-R0 hook (DEC-1013)

processes.name: executor
processes.row: Account executor, one per broker account: Postgres, the vault, its one connection's broker hosts only, and the market-data host until the data service pushes quotes (DEC-2359)

processes.name: token-exchange
processes.row: Token-exchange process (DEC-821 item 2): the vault and DEC-821's one token host, nothing else

processes.name: scheduler
processes.row: Scheduler, one per workspace: the single writer of the hosted workspace's clock stream, whose ticks the runtime and executor the manager starts read (E21-29, DEC-1010); Postgres and time sources, asking none until values.egress.time names one, so every measurement is out of tolerance

processes.name: model-gateway
processes.row: Model gateway, one per workspace: the only caller of a model provider, metering every call on its journaled meter streams before it is sent (E21-62, DEC-2257); Postgres, the vault, and allowed model providers only. It serves `modelGateway.workspace` and, in the cell, the recorded bundle its image carries (`--recorded`), reaching no provider and reading no key (DEC-2326)

processes.name: exporter
processes.row: Cold exporter and anchorer: Postgres, object storage, and the timestamping authority

processes.name: data
processes.row: Market data service, per workspace: its data host only; it serves the workspace's runtimes and executors over the host-local channel, which is not network (§3.1). In the cell, mandate-datad stores each listed instrument's daily bars and its latest trading day's minute bars from the cell's recorded series as mandate-marketdata's datasets under the artifact store, and each instrument's closes object, which the runtime and the executor read read-only; it reaches no host and appends to no stream

postgres.in_cluster: the workspace journal's Postgres pods, port 5432

vault.in_cluster: the vault's pods (V1 and V2), port 8200

model-gateway.in_cluster: the model gateway's pods, port 8080: the runtime's calls, and a replica asking the meter holder to reserve (inference spec §3.6)

broker.external: the connection's paper broker hosts; empty until a lane sets them, and never a live host (DEC-821 item 4)

token-host.external: DEC-821's token host, for the token-exchange process alone

identity-provider.external: the identity provider (OIDC and JWKS, DEC-820)

kube-api.external: the cluster's API server, for the deployment manager alone (DEC-1172): its addresses and port from values, since a policy cannot select the API server by pod label
